Jagjit Singh on 17 December, 2022 In The Court Of Ms. Nabeela Wali Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate-01 New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts: New Delhi In the matter of : Cc No. :- 44283/2016 Food Inspector Department of Pfa Govt of Nct of Delhi A-20 Lawrence Road Industrial Area Delhi-110035 .... Complainant Versus Sh. Jagjit Singh S/o Sh. Kaleecharan M/s Jagjit Halwai, Shop No. 4, Behind Hanuman Mandir, Seva Nagar, New Delhi-110003 R/o H. No. 164, Village Mathana, Distt. Aligarh, U.P. .... Vendor-cum-Proprietor Judgment
texts.facts: The present complaint has been filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 05.11.2010 at about 11:30 AM, Food Inspector (herein after referred to as 'FI') Sh. V.P.S Chaudhary, visited the premises of M/s Jagjit Halwai, Shop No 4, Behind NABEELA NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.12.17 17:21:34 +0530 CC No:- 44283/2016 DA (FSO) v. Jagjit Singh. Page No. 2 of 14 Hanuman Mandir, Seva Nagar, New Delhi-110003 and purchased a sample of Coconut Laddoo for food analysis. The said food article was found stored for sale at the shop. The sample consisting of 1500 gms of Coconut Laddoo was taken from an open tray bearing no label declaration. Vide report dated 20.11.2010, the public analyst reported that the sample is adulterated because it contains added vegetable oil not declared as an ingredient. Subsequently on the basis of the report, the present complaint was filed. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 23.03.2011. 4. On appearing before the court, accused was admitted to bail and provided with copy of complaint. Subsequently vide order dated 09.06.2011 notice under Section 2(1a) (a)(b) & (m) r/w Section 16(1) (a) and Section 7 of PFA Act, 1954 was framed upon the accused, to which he did not plead guilty and claimed trial. COMPLAINANT EVIDENCE 5. At the trial, the complainant department i.e. the prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. by NABE Complainant vs Sh. Jagjit Singh on 17 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105437903/ 2 NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.12 17:21:4 CC No:- 44283/2016 DA (FSO) v. Jagjit Singh. Page No. 3 of 14 6. Sh V.P.S Chaudhary, Food Inspector was examined as PW-1. PW-1 in his examination-in-chief stated that on 05.11.2010 he had visited the shop of the accused where accused Jagjit Singh was found conducting the business of sale of 'Coconut Laddoo'. As per PW-1 after disclosing his identity, he purchased 1500 grams of coconut Laddoo from an open aluminum tub having no label declaration, after properly mixing with the help of clean and dry spoon in a clean and dry tray. As per PW-1 he paid Rs.150/- vide vendors receipt Ex.PW1/A as sample price. As per PW-1 after lifting of sample, it was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed in clean and dry glass bottles. As deposed by PW-1, vendor signatures were obtained on the LHA slip. Thereafter, one counter part of the sample was deposited with the public analyst (PA) on 06.11.2010 and remaining two counterparts were deposited with the LHA. PW-1 further deposed that on receipt of the PA report Ex PW1/H the sample was found to be adulterarted, thereafter he sent a letter ExPW1/H to STO Ward No. 99 to disclose the constitution of M/s Jagjit Halwai shop. As per reply received, no such firm of the accused was found registered with the Sales Tax. PW-1 further deposed that after obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA the present complaint was filed against the accused person. He denied the suggestions that some ghee was present in the tray in which the sample commodity was lying and the same went along with the sample when it was collected. 8. Sh. Shivji Mehto, FA, who was part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings was examined as PW-2. PW-2 deposed on similar lines as PW-1 and identified his signatures on relevant documents. PW-2 however, could not be cross- NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.12.17 17:21:58 +0530 CC No:- 44283/2016 DA (FSO) v. Jagjit Singh . Page examined as he had expired. 9. Sh.P.R. Jha, then SDM/LHA, who was part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings was examined as PW-3. PW-3 deposed on similar lines as PW-1 and identified his signatures on the relevant documents. PW-3 was cross examined by counsel for the accused. No other witness was examined and complainant's evidence was then closed. EXAMINATION OF ACCUSED U/S 313/281 CRPC 10. Thereafter, all the incriminating evidence was put to the accused person and his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused Jagjit Singh admitted the sample proceedings as well as receiving the letter Ex.PW1/L. He however choose not to lead any defence evidence. ARGUMENTS 11.
texts.arguments: Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as all the witnesses have supported the case and there is no contradiction in their testimony. It is further submitted that the accused has failed to rebut the findings as given by the PA in his report Ex.PW1/G and neither the said NABEELA WALI WALI CC Complainant vs Sh. Jagjit Singh on 17 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105437903/ 4 No:- 44283/2016 DA (FSO) v. Jagjit Singh. 2022.12.17 +0530 report has been challenged. 12. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for the accused that the food article i.e. Coconut Laddu would fall under the category of sweet as mentioned under Appendix B of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rule 1995 under the heading of "A.25 SWEETS AND CONFECTIONERY". It is further argued that since the said category of food permits the usage of edible oils and fats hence there was no occasion for the Public Analyst to test the product for vegetable oil. Also it is argued that it was wrongly concluded that the food product in question was adulterated because of the presence of the vegetable oil, as vegetable oil is not injurious to health. It is also argued by Ld. Counsel for the accused the the BR test conducted by the Food Analyst is prescribed only to find out the adulteration in vegetable oils. It is argued that since edible oils including vegetable oil is permitted in sweets, hence the test was wrongly applied by the Food Analyst. 13. It is also argued by Ld. Counsel for the accused person that it is not clear as to how the Food Analyst came to know about the ingredients of the food article, as copy of Form VI which mentions the constituents of the food article as declared by the accused was not provided to the Food Analyst and only Form VII as per rules was sent to the Food Analyst. It is further argued that as per circular dated 19.07.2021 FSSAI coconut ladoo can only be tested for contaminants, microbiological requirements and additives allowed to be used. Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be.
